name: wm8900_hp_event
prose: DAPM event handler for the WM8900 headphone widget: w is the widget, kcontrol unused, event the DAPM event. It reads WM8900_REG_HPCTL1 into hpctl1 and then switches on the event; it returns 0 on its only return, for all events. PRE_PMU writes HPCTL1 with only the input and output clamp bits set. POST_PMU clears the input clamp, sets HP_SHORT, HP_SHORT2 and the input stage enable and writes; waits 400 ms; clears the output clamp, sets the output stage enable and writes; clears HP_SHORT2 and writes; clears HP_SHORT and writes. PRE_PMD sets HP_SHORT and writes; clears the output stage enable and writes; sets both clamps, clears the input stage enable and writes. POST_PMD writes 0 to HPCTL1. Any other event triggers a WARN and nothing is written.
note: Listed as the unnamed tail of a DAPM headphone event handler (dropped); the function is wm8900_hp_event, wm8900.c:221-284, a real function, so fixed. Register write results are not checked.

name: wsa884x_get_temp
prose: Precondition: wsa884x is the driver data, temp points to a long for the result in thousandths of a degree. Takes wsa884x->sp_lock with a scope guard, so the mutex is released automatically on every return. If wsa884x->pa_on is set it returns the cached wsa884x->temperature * 1000 in *temp and 0 (no hardware access). Otherwise it calls pm_runtime_resume_and_get and returns its negative error if it fails (no runtime-PM reference is held then). It then sets the PA FSM bypass bits, toggles TEMP_VALUE_RD_EN around reading the measured TEMP_DIN MSB/LSB registers, reads four OTP registers (all regmap read and update results are ignored), clears the bypass bits, and forms 10-bit values dmeas, d1 and d2. If d1 equals d2 it sets -EINVAL. Otherwise it computes val = T1 + (dmeas - d1) * (T2 - T1) / (d2 - d1); if val is strictly between WSA884X_LOW_TEMP_THRESHOLD and WSA884X_HIGH_TEMP_THRESHOLD it stores it in wsa884x->temperature, sets *temp = val * 1000 and the result 0, else the result is -EAGAIN (*temp unchanged). On every path after a successful runtime resume it calls pm_runtime_put_autosuspend before returning that result.
note: slice cut the head; real function wsa884x.c:1862-1947. Reviewer WRONG: the mutex is taken with guard(mutex) (line 1871), which releases it automatically at every return, including the out path; no explicit unlock is needed.

name: dw_i2s_hw_params
prose: Precondition: substream, params and dai belong to a DesignWare I2S device. Returns 0 or a negative error. It maps the format to settings stored in the device: S16_LE gives data_width 16, ccr 0x00, xfer_resolution 0x02; S24_LE gives 24, 0x08, 0x04; S32_LE gives 32, 0x10, 0x05; any other format logs and returns -EINVAL before modifying anything. If dev->tdm_slots is set data_width is forced to 32. It stores the channel count in config->chan_nr and returns -EINVAL for a count other than the 2, 4, 6 or 8 supported values (this return happens after data_width, ccr, xfer_resolution and chan_nr have already been updated, so those fields are not unchanged on that error). Then it calls dw_i2s_config(dev, stream), writes dev->ccr to the CCR register and stores the sample rate. If the device has DW_I2S_MASTER capability it configures the clock: with an i2s_clk_cfg callback it calls it and returns its negative result; otherwise it calls clk_set_rate with rate * data_width * 2 and returns a nonzero error. It returns 0.
note: dwc-i2s.c:274-347 (slice cut the head). Reviewer right: the -EINVAL for the channel count comes after config and device fields were modified (lines 283-308, then 316-318).

name: fsl_asoc_card_probe
prose: Platform probe of the Freescale generic ASoC card; pdev is the platform device. Returns 0 or a negative error. It devm-allocates the private data (-ENOMEM if that fails, nothing else to undo). It finds the CPU DAI node (audio-cpu, falling back to ssi-controller and spdif-controller; -EINVAL if none, via fail) and the CPU platform device (-EPROBE_DEFER via fail if not found). From here on every failure and the successful path go through the asrc_fail label, which drops references (of_node_put on asrc_np and both codec nodes and put_device on the CPU device) and then through fail (of_node_put on cpu_np). It looks up up to two codec nodes and their I2C or platform devices, the optional ASRC device, and each codec's MCLK rate; sets defaults, copies the DAI link templates, allocates 10 DAI link components (-ENOMEM) and wires the links. It selects the codec DAI name and per-card options by device-tree compatible: an unknown compatible logs and returns -EINVAL, and the SPDIF compatible calls fsl_asoc_card_spdif_init (its error is returned). It reads optional mclk-id and clock-provider format settings from DT (releasing the provider node refs), returns -EPROBE_DEFER if a non-AC97 codec device is missing, runs CPU-specific setup (audmux init failure returns its error; an ESAI clock deferral returns -EPROBE_DEFER), parses the card name and optional audio-routing (parse failure returned), fills the link components (an AC97 card needs a CPU cell-index, else the error is returned; allocation failure -ENOMEM), adds the DPCM links and reads the ASRC rate and format properties when an ASRC exists (missing properties return -EINVAL), sets driver data, registers the card with devm_snd_soc_register_card (error returned) and creates the optional headphone and mic jacks (errors returned). Parts of the function between lines 905-930 and 1008-1035 were skimmed, not read line by line. The success path also executes the reference drops above and returns 0.
note: slice cut the head; real function fsl-asoc-card.c:618-1083. Reviewer right: the asrc_fail path (1074-1078) releases the of_parse_phandle references with of_node_put, and the same code runs on success. References from of_find_device_by_node / of_find_i2c_device_by_node are not released in this function (not read further).

name: asrc_m2m_device_run
prose: Precondition: pair is a configured ASRC pair and task carries input_size and receives output_size. Returns 0 or a negative error. If the ASRC has m2m_set_ratio_mod and pair->ratio_mod_flag is set it applies the ratio modifier and clears the flag. It takes the input and output DMA buffers, computes the input sample width and FIFO address, and returns -EINVAL (logged) if the input size is smaller than one frame, larger than ASRC_M2M_BUFFER_SIZE, or not a multiple of the frame size. It configures the input DMA with asrc_dmaconfig and returns that function's nonzero result if it fails (this includes any error asrc_dmaconfig returns, such as an allocation failure). It computes the output length with m2m_calc_out_len; if it is positive and within ASRC_M2M_BUFFER_SIZE it configures the output DMA (error returned), if it is above the buffer size it returns -EINVAL, and if it is 0 no output DMA is configured. It then re-initialises both completions, submits and issues the input DMA (and the output DMA if out_dma_len > 0), starts the ASRC, and waits up to 10 seconds for the input completion and, if output is expected, for the output completion; a zero return from wait_for_completion_interruptible_timeout gives -ETIMEDOUT (a negative return because of a signal is not treated as an error by this check). On success it reads the last FIFO words (which can update out_dma_len), stores the length in task->output_size and returns 0. Nothing is cleaned up on the error paths here, and output_size is only set on success.
note: slice cut the head; real function fsl_asrc_m2m.c:186-286. Reviewer right: errors from asrc_dmaconfig (including -ENOMEM) are propagated by the two 'if (ret) goto end' paths (228-231, 243-246); asrc_dmaconfig itself not read.

name: fsl_sai_probe
prose: Platform probe of the NXP SAI controller; pdev is the platform device. Returns 0 on success or a negative error. Failures before runtime PM is enabled just return the error with no PM cleanup: devm allocation (-ENOMEM), ioremap of resource 0, regmap init, the bus clock (also an old "sai" name fallback), fsl_sai_read_dlcfg, platform_get_irq, devm_request_irq, -EINVAL when both fsl,sai-synchronous-rx and fsl,sai-asynchronous are present, the iomuxc syscon lookup and of_alias_get_id for i.MX6UL with MCLK output. Before those it also gets the mclk1..mclk(MAX-1) clocks (a failed one is set to NULL and only logged), fills mclk0 from mclk1 or the bus clock, PLL clocks and rate constraints, multi-FIFO DMA detection, the synchronous or asynchronous TX/RX configuration and the DMA parameters. After platform_set_drvdata it calls pm_runtime_enable; if runtime PM is not enabled it calls fsl_sai_runtime_resume directly (failure goes to err_pm_disable). It then takes a runtime PM reference (pm_runtime_resume_and_get), reads the version (a failure is only a warning), enables the MCLK output bit when requested and supported, and drops the reference with pm_runtime_put_sync (a negative value other than -ENOSYS fails). It registers the PCM (imx_pcm_dma_init, or devm_snd_dmaengine_pcm_register) and the ASoC component with devm_snd_soc_register_component. Any failure from the resume-and-get onward goes to err_pm_get_sync, which calls fsl_sai_runtime_suspend if the device is not runtime-suspended, and then to err_pm_disable, which calls pm_runtime_disable; both return the saved error. On success it returns 0.
note: slice cut the head; real function fsl_sai.c:1442-1656. Reviewer right: the early returns (IRQ at 1526-1535, DT conflict 1551, syscon 1574, alias 1579) come before pm_runtime_enable (1595) so they do no runtime-PM cleanup; only failures after that point do.

name: avs_path_pause
prose: Precondition: path is an avs path whose owner avs_dev is valid; the caller must not hold adev->path_mutex, because avs_condpaths_pause takes and releases that mutex. Returns 0 immediately if path->state is already AVS_PPL_STATE_PAUSED. Otherwise it calls avs_condpaths_pause(adev, path), which pauses the attached conditional paths under adev->path_mutex, then walks path->ppl_list in reverse and sets each pipeline to AVS_PPL_STATE_PAUSED with avs_ipc_set_pipeline_state; on the first nonzero result it logs, sets path->state to AVS_PPL_STATE_INVALID and returns AVS_IPC_RET(ret) (pipelines already paused stay paused). If all succeed it sets path->state to AVS_PPL_STATE_PAUSED and returns 0.
note: slice cut the head; real function path.c:1505-1528. Reviewer right: avs_condpaths_pause locks adev->path_mutex (1494-1502), so a caller holding it would deadlock.

name: avs_dai_nonhda_be_trigger
prose: Precondition: substream and dai belong to a non-HDA back-end whose avs_dma_data (path) was set with the DAI. Returns 0 (the initial ret) or a value from the path calls. RESUME with the dai link's ignore_suspend set does nothing and returns 0; otherwise RESUME, START and PAUSE_RELEASE call avs_path_pause(data->path) (a negative result is logged and returned, without running) and then avs_path_run(data->path, AVS_TPLG_TRIGGER_AUTO), whose result is returned (negative results logged). SUSPEND with ignore_suspend set does nothing and returns 0; otherwise SUSPEND, PAUSE_PUSH and STOP call avs_path_pause (result logged if negative) and then avs_path_reset, and the return value is the result of avs_path_reset (so a pause failure is only logged and is overwritten by the reset result). Any other cmd returns -EINVAL.
note: pcm.c:269-317. Reviewer right: the return value is the avs_path_run / avs_path_reset result and can be negative (lines 291, 306, 316).

name: avs_dai_hda_be_trigger
prose: Precondition: substream and dai belong to an HDA back-end whose avs_dma_data holds the path and link_stream. Returns 0 or a value from the path calls. RESUME with ignore_suspend set returns 0 without action; otherwise RESUME, START and PAUSE_RELEASE start the link stream with snd_hdac_ext_stream_start, call avs_path_pause (negative result logged and returned without running) and then avs_path_run(..., AVS_TPLG_TRIGGER_AUTO), whose result is returned. SUSPEND with ignore_suspend set returns 0 without action; otherwise SUSPEND, PAUSE_PUSH and STOP call avs_path_pause (negative result only logged), clear the link stream with snd_hdac_ext_stream_clear and call avs_path_reset, and the return value is the avs_path_reset result (an earlier pause failure is overwritten). Any other cmd returns -EINVAL. A debug message is printed on entry.
note: pcm.c:488-542 (slice cut the head). Reviewer right: the return value is the avs_path_run / avs_path_reset result and can be negative (lines 514, 531, 541).

name: avs_module_ida_alloc
prose: Precondition: adev is the avs device with mods_info and mod_idas possibly set, newinfo describes the new module count, purge says whether existing IDAs are discarded. If purge is false and old info exists it remembers tocopy_count = oldinfo->count and warns when the old count is not below the new count. It allocates an array of newinfo->count IDA pointers (kcalloc) and returns -ENOMEM if that fails, leaving adev->mod_idas untouched. If tocopy_count is nonzero it memcpy's that many old pointers into the new array (the memcpy count is not clamped to newinfo->count). For each index from tocopy_count up to newinfo->count it allocates and initialises an IDA; on a kzalloc failure it frees only the IDAs allocated in this call (indices from tocopy_count below the failing one are freed together with indices below tocopy_count when the loop decrements down to 0, because while (i--) frees every index from i-1 down to 0), then frees the new array and returns -ENOMEM; adev->mod_idas is left unchanged. On success, if tocopy_count is nonzero it frees only the old pointer array (the IDAs are reused), otherwise it calls avs_module_ida_destroy(adev) to destroy the old IDAs; then it stores the new array in adev->mod_idas and returns 0.
note: utils.c:112-155. Reviewer right that on the kcalloc failure nothing is freed and old IDAs remain valid (lines 127-129). Note for the failing kzalloc path: while (i--) frees from i-1 down to 0, which includes the reused old pointers copied in at index < tocopy_count (those belong to the old array and are still referenced by adev->mod_idas), so that path can free IDAs that adev->mod_idas still points to when tocopy_count is nonzero.

name: mt8186_afe_enable_clock
prose: Precondition: afe is the MT8186 AFE with platform_priv holding the clocks. Returns 0 or the first error. It enables in order CLK_INFRA_SYS_AUDIO, CLK_INFRA_AUDIO_26M, CLK_MUX_AUDIO (prepare_enable; then sets its parent to CLK_CLK26M) and CLK_MUX_AUDIOINTBUS (prepare_enable), sets the audio internal bus parent to CLK_TOP_MAINPLL_D2_D4 with mt8186_set_audio_int_bus_parent, sets the parent of CLK_TOP_MUX_AUDIO_H to CLK_TOP_APLL2_CK (clk_set_parent only; that clock is not prepared or enabled here) and prepare_enables CLK_AFE; then returns 0. On a failure it jumps to a label and falls through the following ones: AFE enable failure disables CLK_AFE; the MUX_AUDIO_H parent or the intbus parent failure sets the internal bus parent back to CLK_CLK26M; then MUX_AUDIOINTBUS is disabled, then MUX_AUDIO, then INFRA_SYS_AUDIO, then INFRA_AUDIO_26M. The unwinding labels are not exact mirrors of the enable order: a failure of the first enable (INFRA_SYS_AUDIO) jumps to a label that disables INFRA_SYS_AUDIO and then INFRA_AUDIO_26M, neither of which was enabled, and a failure of the second (INFRA_AUDIO_26M) jumps to the last label which disables only INFRA_AUDIO_26M, leaving INFRA_SYS_AUDIO enabled.
note: slice cut the head; real function mt8186-afe-clk.c:240-318. Reviewer right: CLK_TOP_MUX_AUDIO_H only has its parent set (285-292), it is never prepared or enabled in this function. The label-order observation is from my own reading of 245-317.

name: mt8188_mt6359_mtkaif_calibration
prose: Precondition: rtd is the card's PCM runtime. Returns -EINVAL if the AFE component is not found; otherwise it returns 0 on every other path, including calibration failure and a missing topckgen (calibration failure is recorded only in the stored parameters). It resets the stored mtkaif parameters (calibration_ok false, chosen_phase -1, phase_cycle 0 for each MISO). If afe_priv->topckgen is an error pointer it logs and returns 0 at that point. Otherwise it finds the "MTKAIF_PIN" widget; if found it sends it SND_SOC_DAPM_PRE_PMU through snd_soc_dapm_pinctrl_event. It takes a runtime PM reference (pm_runtime_get_sync), enables the mt6359 calibration and selects the synchroniser-pulse test. For phase 0 to 42, while no error occurred, it sets the codec phases, starts the test, and polls CKSYS_AUD_TOP_MON until both done bits are set or 10000 polls pass (then it logs and clears the ok flag); it records the first cycle value as the reference at phase 0, and when a MISO's cycle differs from the reference for the first time it stores phase - 1 as its chosen phase and the reference cycle as its phase cycle; it stops the test pulse and leaves the loop once both chosen phases are set. A missing chosen phase makes the calibration not ok and uses phase 0. It sets the codec to the two chosen phases (third 0), disables the mt6359 calibration, drops the runtime PM reference with pm_runtime_put, stores the ok flag, both chosen phases and the phase cycles in the stored parameters, sends the pin widget SND_SOC_DAPM_POST_PMD if it exists, and returns 0.
note: slice cut the head; real function mt8188-mt6359.c:357-519. Reviewer WRONG: the code does send SND_SOC_DAPM_POST_PMD (line 513) and does store phase cycles (509-510).

name: mtk_adda_ch34_ul_event
prose: DAPM event handler for the MT8192 ADDA CH34 uplink widget: w is the widget, kcontrol unused. Returns 0 for every event (its only return). It copies afe_priv->mtkaif_dmic_ch34 into the local mtkaif_dmic and afe_priv->mtkaif_adda6_only into the local mtkaif_adda6_only. SND_SOC_DAPM_PRE_PMU requests the CH34 gpios (mt8192_afe_gpio_request true); if the local mtkaif_dmic is nonzero it sets bit 0 of AFE_ADDA6_MTKAIF_RX_CFG0, clears the voice-mode field of that register and calls mtk_adda_ul_src_dmic for CH34; if mtkaif_adda6_only is nonzero it sets bit 23 of AFE_ADDA_MTKAIF_SYNCWORD_CFG. SND_SOC_DAPM_POST_PMD sleeps 125-135 us, releases the CH34 gpios (request false), sets afe_priv->mtkaif_dmic_ch34 back to 0, and, if the local mtkaif_adda6_only is nonzero, clears bit 23 of the syncword register. Other events do nothing.
note: slice cut the head; real function mt8192-dai-adda.c:251-311. Reviewer MIXED: the code tests the local mtkaif_dmic, but that local is initialised from afe_priv->mtkaif_dmic_ch34 (line 258); the claim that mtkaif_adda6_only is not a platform_priv field is wrong: it is read from afe_priv at line 259.

name: mt8192_mt6359_mtkaif_calibration
prose: Precondition: rtd is the card's PCM runtime; the AFE component lookup result is not checked for NULL. Returns 0 on its only return. It takes a runtime PM reference (pm_runtime_get_sync), requests the ADDA and ADDA CH34 gpios, enables the mt6359 calibration, programs AFE_AUD_PAD_TOP for clock protocol 2 and sets the topckgen test type to the synchroniser pulse. It sets mtkaif_calibration_num_phase to 42 and resets the three chosen phases in afe_priv to -1. For phase 0 to 42 while no timeout occurred it sets the three codec phases, starts the test, and polls CKSYS_AUD_TOP_MON until all three done bits are set or more than 10000 polls (then it logs and stops the loop with the failure flag). The cycle values stay -1 for a channel whose done bit was never seen. It takes the phase-0 cycles as references and, after each phase, stores phase - 1 as the chosen phase (and the reference cycle as phase cycle) for each channel whose cycle differs from its reference and is still unset; this check also runs after a timeout, so a channel whose cycle is -1 on a timeout can get a chosen phase. It stops the test pulse and leaves the loop early once all three chosen phases are set. Any phase still unset is replaced by 0 for the final programming of the codec phases; afe_priv->mtkaif_chosen_phase keeps -1 for unset ones. It then disables the rx fifo, disables the mt6359 calibration, releases the gpios, calls pm_runtime_put, logs and returns 0.
note: mt8192-mt6359-rt1015-rt5682.c:150-305 (slice cut the head). Reviewer right: the compare against prev_cycle at 240-256 runs after the timeout break, so chosen_phase can be set even then. The calibration failure is not reported in the return value.

name: get_etdm_fs_timing
prose: Pure lookup: scans mt8195_etdm_rates in order and returns the reg_value of the first entry whose rate equals rate, or -EINVAL if no entry matches. No side effects.
note: mt8195-dai-etdm.c:172-181. Reviewer mechanical (contract omits EINVAL): right; contract left empty.

name: lpass_cpu_daiops_hw_params
prose: Precondition: substream, params and dai belong to a qcom LPASS MI2S DAI. Returns 0 or a negative error, with the earlier register writes left in place on an error. It computes the sample bit width with snd_pcm_format_width and returns its negative result if it is negative. It writes the loopback field (disabled) and the wssrc field (internal), returning any error, then maps the width (16, 24 or 32; anything else returns -EINVAL) to the bitwidth field and writes it. It takes the stream's SD line mode from drvdata (mi2s_playback_sd_mode or mi2s_capture_sd_mode for this id) and returns -EINVAL if it is 0. It then adjusts the mode for the channel count: 1 or 2 channels map the multi-line modes to SD0 (QUAD01, 6CH, 8CH) or SD2 (QUAD23); 4 channels require mode >= QUAD01 and map 6CH and 8CH to QUAD01; 6 channels require mode >= 6CH and map 8CH to 6CH; 8 channels require mode >= 8CH; each failing requirement and any other channel count return -EINVAL. For playback it writes the speaker mode and speaker mono/stereo fields, for capture the mic mode and mic mono/stereo fields (stereo when channels >= 2); errors are returned. Finally it sets the MI2S bit clock to rate * bitwidth * 2 with clk_set_rate (error returned) and returns 0. This function does not write the speaker or microphone enable fields.
note: lpass-cpu.c:134-297 (slice cut the head). Reviewer MIXED: right that -EINVAL is returned for invalid width, mode and channels (so no such precondition is needed), wrong that spken/micen enable writes were omitted: this function contains no such writes.

name: q6apm_dai_compr_set_params
prose: Precondition: component, stream and params for a compress stream whose runtime->private_data is a q6apm_dai_rtd. Returns 0 or a negative error. It returns -EINVAL at once, before touching prtd, if snd_soc_component_get_drvdata gives NULL. Otherwise it stores periods (fragments), pcm_count (fragment size), pcm_size and bits_per_sample = 16 in prtd. If prtd->next_track is not true it copies the codec parameters into prtd->codec, calls q6apm_set_real_module_id (nonzero result returned), builds a config (direction, sample rate, 2 channels, 16 bits, format = codec id, default channel map, codec) and calls q6apm_graph_media_format_shmem (negative result returned), q6apm_graph_media_format_pcm (nonzero returned), q6apm_map_memory_regions on playback with the pcm region split into periods (a negative result returns -ENOMEM), q6apm_graph_prepare and q6apm_graph_start (nonzero results returned). If next_track is true it builds a similar config and calls audioreach_compr_set_param (negative result returned). On success it sets prtd->state to Q6APM_STREAM_RUNNING and returns 0. A failure after the prtd fields were stored leaves them stored; nothing is undone on error.
note: slice cut the head; real function q6apm-dai.c:646-720. Reviewer right: the NULL drvdata -EINVAL (659-660) returns before any prtd field is stored (662-665), so those fields are not stored on every path.

name: soc_compr_open_fe
prose: Precondition: cstream->private_data is a front-end snd_soc_pcm_runtime. Returns 0 or a negative error. It takes the card mutex, calls dpcm_path_get (on failure it goes to be_err, which sets the FE stream runtime_update to SND_SOC_DPCM_UPDATE_NO, unlocks the card mutex and returns the error; no path list was obtained). Otherwise it takes the DPCM mutex, adds the valid BE paths (dpcm_add_paths), sets runtime_update to FE and starts the BEs with dpcm_be_dai_startup; if that fails it marks all BE links SND_SOC_DPCM_LINK_STATE_FREE, calls dpcm_be_disconnect and goes to out. Then it starts the CPU DAI (snd_soc_dai_compr_startup; failure goes to out), opens the components (snd_soc_compr_components_open; failure goes to open_err), and starts the machine link (snd_soc_link_compr_startup; failure goes to machine_err). On success it clears the pending DPCM state, puts the path list, sets the FE state to SND_SOC_DPCM_STATE_OPEN and runtime_update to NO, activates the runtime, unlocks both mutexes and returns 0. The error labels fall through: machine_err frees the components (snd_soc_compr_components_free(cstream, 1)), then open_err shuts down the CPU DAI (snd_soc_dai_compr_shutdown(..., 1)), then out puts the path list and unlocks the DPCM mutex, then be_err as above; each returns the saved ret. A components_open failure goes to open_err, so snd_soc_compr_components_free is not called from here in that case.
note: soc-compress.c:133-201. Reviewer MIXED: right that a components_open failure does no components_free at this level (169-171 jump to open_err), but wrong that link-startup rollback is missing: machine_err (190-191) frees the components and open_err shuts down the CPU DAI.

name: snd_soc_daifmt_clock_provider_flipped
prose: Pure helper: returns dai_fmt with its clock-provider field (mask SND_SOC_DAIFMT_CLOCK_PROVIDER_MASK, 0xf000) swapped for the opposite role and all other bits unchanged. Within that field SND_SOC_DAIFMT_CBP_CFP (1 << 12) becomes SND_SOC_DAIFMT_CBC_CFC (4 << 12), CBC_CFC becomes CBP_CFP, CBP_CFC (3 << 12) becomes CBC_CFP (2 << 12) and CBC_CFP becomes CBP_CFC. If the field holds any other value (including 0) the provider field of the result is 0, because the field is cleared first and nothing is ORed in. No side effects.
note: soc-core.c:3292-3312; constants checked in include/sound/soc-dai.h:116-119 and 138. Reviewer MIXED: right that the mask is 0xf000, but its stated mapping (0x1000<->0x2000, 0x3000<->0x4000) is wrong; the code maps 0x1000<->0x4000 and 0x3000<->0x2000.

name: dpcm_fe_dai_startup
prose: Precondition: fe_substream is a front-end substream. Sets the FE update state to SND_SOC_DPCM_UPDATE_FE, then calls dpcm_be_dai_startup(fe, stream); on a negative result it jumps to be_err, skipping the unwind (the BE startup is assumed to clean up after itself; its internals were not read). Otherwise it opens the FE with __soc_pcm_open; a failure goes to unwind. On success it sets the FE state to SND_SOC_DPCM_STATE_OPEN, runs dpcm_runtime_setup_fe and the three BE runtime setup helpers for format, channels and rate (what they actually constrain depends on those helpers; they were not read), and sets ret = dpcm_apply_symmetry. At unwind, if ret is negative it calls dpcm_be_dai_startup_unwind(fe, stream); this function does not itself close the FE in that case. At be_err it sets the FE update state back to SND_SOC_DPCM_UPDATE_NO and returns soc_pcm_ret(fe, ret) (ret, after any logging that helper does).
note: slice cut the head; real function soc-pcm.c:1946-1981. Reviewer right: a dpcm_be_dai_startup failure goes to be_err and skips the unwind (1953-1955); the old 'always unwind' claim was wrong. Helper internals not read, so the 'no-ops without dpcm_merged_*' part is unverified.

name: dpcm_be_dai_trigger
prose: Precondition: fe is the front-end runtime, stream the direction, cmd a PCM trigger command. Walks the front end's BE list; for each BE it takes the BE substream's stream lock (irqsave) and skips the BE (goto next) if snd_soc_dpcm_can_be_update says this op is not for it. For START it skips unless be_start is set or the BE state is PREPARE, STOP or PAUSED; it increments be_start and acts only when the count becomes 1, triggering PAUSE_RELEASE if the state was PAUSED or START otherwise. RESUME acts only from state SUSPEND, with the same be_start counting. PAUSE_RELEASE clears fe_pause, decrements be_pause and then counts and triggers like START. STOP acts only from START or PAUSED, decrements be_start for START and acts when it reaches 0, handles the fe_pause / be_pause bookkeeping and triggers PAUSE_PUSH if be_pause is nonzero, else STOP. SUSPEND acts only from START and triggers when be_start drops to 0. PAUSE_PUSH acts only from START, sets fe_pause, increments be_pause and triggers when be_start drops to 0. If soc_pcm_trigger returns nonzero the counters changed for that command are reverted (be_start, and for STOP the pause bookkeeping) and the BE state is left unchanged; on success the BE state becomes START, SUSPEND, PAUSED or STOP according to the command. After each BE the stream lock is released and, if ret is nonzero, the loop stops (the remaining BEs are not visited). It returns soc_pcm_ret(fe, ret), so ret is passed through that helper, not returned bare. Commands not listed leave ret 0.
note: slice cut the head; real function soc-pcm.c:2184-2351. Reviewer WRONG on both points: after a failed trigger the code goes to next (unlock) and then breaks out of the loop (2347-2348), and the return is soc_pcm_ret(fe, ret) (2350).

name: dpcm_run_update_startup
prose: Precondition: fe is the front-end runtime in the middle of a runtime update, stream the direction. Returns 0 or a negative error through soc_pcm_ret(fe, ret) at the end (the early success returns return 0 directly). If the FE state is SND_SOC_DPCM_STATE_HW_FREE or STATE_CLOSE it logs and sets -EINVAL, going to disconnect. Otherwise it calls dpcm_be_dai_startup (a negative result goes to disconnect directly, skipping hw_free and shutdown), returns 0 if the FE state is OPEN, calls dpcm_be_dai_hw_params (failure goes to close), returns 0 if the FE state is HW_PARAMS, calls dpcm_be_dai_prepare (failure goes to hw_free), runs a NOP DAPM stream event, returns 0 if the FE state is PREPARE or STOP, then calls dpcm_be_dai_trigger with START (failure goes to hw_free) and returns 0. The error labels fall through: hw_free calls dpcm_be_dai_hw_free, close calls dpcm_be_dai_shutdown, disconnect then walks the BE list and, for each BE that can be updated and is in state CLOSE or NEW, sets that link's state to SND_SOC_DPCM_LINK_STATE_FREE, and the function returns soc_pcm_ret(fe, ret). The disconnect step also runs when the FE state is invalid.
note: slice cut the head; real function soc-pcm.c:2564-2635. Reviewer right: the invalid-state path still runs the disconnect loop (2578), and a dpcm_be_dai_startup failure jumps straight to disconnect (2584) skipping hw_free and shutdown.

name: hda_dsp_core_run
prose: Precondition: sdev is the SOF device, core_mask selects DSP cores. It calls hda_dsp_core_reset_leave(sdev, core_mask) and returns its negative result at once if it is negative. Then it clears the stall bits for core_mask in HDA_DSP_REG_ADSPCS (snd_sof_dsp_update_bits_unlocked). If hda_dsp_core_is_enabled says the cores are not running it calls hda_dsp_core_stall_reset(sdev, core_mask), logs an error and sets ret to -EIO. It returns ret (0 when the cores are enabled; a non-negative value from reset_leave is passed through as ret if it was positive).
note: slice cut the head; real function hda-dsp.c:247-272. Reviewer WRONG: hda_dsp_core_stall_reset is called on the failure path (line 265) before -EIO is set.

name: hda_dsp_ipc4_pm_msg
prose: Static inline predicate on the primary word of an IPC4 message: returns false unless the message's target bit (bit 30, SOF_IPC4_MSG_IS_MODULE_MSG) equals SOF_IPC4_MODULE_MSG, the module-message value (the second enumerator of enum sof_ipc4_msg_target, i.e. 1); for a module message it returns true when the 5-bit type field (bits 24 to 28) equals SOF_IPC4_MOD_SET_DX or SOF_IPC4_MOD_SET_D0IX, and false for any other type. No side effects.
note: hda-ipc.c:77-88; macros checked in include/sound/sof/ipc4/header.h:76-83 and 149-165. Reviewer WRONG: enum sof_ipc4_msg_target has SOF_IPC4_FW_GEN_MSG = 0 and SOF_IPC4_MODULE_MSG = 1 (header.h:77-83), so the module target value is 1, not 2.

name: hda_dsp_cl_boot_firmware
prose: Precondition: sdev is a SOF Intel HDA device with a base firmware loaded in sdev->basefw. If IMR boot is supported, this is not the first boot and skip_imr_boot is clear, it resets boot_iteration to 0 and tries hda_dsp_boot_imr; on success it sets booted_from_imr and returns 0 (not the core mask); on failure it warns and cold boots. It sets booted_from_imr false and returns -EINVAL if the base firmware size is not larger than its payload offset. It initialises the boot wait queue, prepares the code-loader DMA stream with hda_cl_prepare (returning PTR_ERR on failure; nothing to clean up yet), and copies the payload into the DMA buffer when the buffer is temporary or does not already hold the base firmware. It then tries chip_info->cl_init up to HDA_FW_BOOT_ATTEMPTS times (setting boot_iteration each time; -EINVAL if cl_init is not set), stopping at the first success; if all attempts fail it logs and goes to cleanup with that last error. After a successful ROM init it processes SoundWire wake-ups when this is not the first boot, sets boot_iteration to HDA_FW_BOOT_ATTEMPTS, and copies the firmware with hda_cl_copy_fw: on success skip_imr_boot is set to false, on failure a debug dump is taken and skip_imr_boot is set to true. At cleanup it always calls hda_cl_cleanup; a negative cleanup result is logged and replaces ret only if ret was 0. If ret is 0 it returns chip_info->init_core_mask. Otherwise it disables the DSP PPCAP (hda_dsp_ctrl_ppcap_enable(sdev, false)) and returns ret. So PPCAP is disabled only on the failure return.
note: slice cut the head; real function hda-loader.c:427-569. Reviewer MIXED: right that skip_imr_boot is set to true on failure (539); wrong that the function returns ret rather than init_core_mask (562-563 returns init_core_mask on success) and wrong that PPCAP is disabled unconditionally (566 is only reached when ret is nonzero).

name: sof_ipc4_prepare_copier_module
prose: Precondition: swidget is a copier-type widget (host aif in/out, DAI in/out or buffer) with a valid pipeline; fe_params and pipeline_params are hw params, platform_params carries the stream tag, dir the stream direction. Returns 0 or a negative error. Early returns: -EINVAL for any other widget id (first switch); for aif widgets the error from sof_update_ipc_object of the deep-buffer token; for aif widgets using chain DMA it sets the chain-DMA fields of the pipeline message (host id, SCS bit for 16-bit, FIFO size), sets copier_data->gtw_cfg.node_id to SOF_IPC4_CHAIN_DMA_NODE_ID and returns 0 without further preparation; for DAI widgets using chain DMA it returns 0 at once; -ENOMEM if kmemdup of the reference hw params fails; for DAI widgets the error of sof_ipc4_prepare_dai_copier. It builds ref_params from fe_params (aif playback, DAI) or pipeline_params (aif capture, buffer; DAI playback re-copies pipeline_params into it after the DAI preparation), sets the host node index from the stream tag for aif widgets, and calls sof_ipc4_init_input_audio_fmt (a negative index is returned). It determines the output reference rate, channels, type and valid bits from the chosen input format (aif in, DAI out, buffer) or from fe_params (aif out, DAI in; errors from the sample type and valid bits helpers are returned), or from the single output format if the copier has only one output bit depth; then calls sof_ipc4_init_output_audio_fmt (a negative index is returned) and copies the chosen output format into copier_data->out_format. For ALH DAI widgets it builds the ALH blob: it counts channels from the channel map, derives the per-device channel masks and mappings by walking the matching ALH DAI widgets of the same stream name, and for more than one device allocates a group id with ida_alloc_max (a negative result is returned) and puts it in the node id. It then calls sof_ipc4_update_hw_params on pipeline_params (nonzero result returned), sets the gateway DMA buffer size by widget type (the aif-in case uses the larger of the minimum and the deep-buffer milliseconds), computes the IPC size as the copier data, the gateway config and the DMA-config TLVs, allocates ipc_config_data with kzalloc (-ENOMEM on failure; the previous pointer is not freed here), records the size, updates resource usage, copies the pieces into the buffer and restores gtw_cfg.config_length before returning 0. ref_params is freed automatically at every return.
note: Listed as a fragment (dropped); the slice (ipc4-topology.c:2050-2302) lies inside sof_ipc4_prepare_copier_module (2002-2469), a real function, so fixed. Read with comments and debug lines filtered out; the ALH mapping details (2263-2368) were summarised, not verified line by line; callee helpers not read. The old prose said ref_params may leak: it is declared with __free(kfree) (line 2013), so it is freed on every return.

name: sof_ipc4_control_setup
prose: Dispatcher on scontrol->info_type. SND_SOC_TPLG_CTL_VOLSW, VOLSW_SX and VOLSW_XR_SX return sof_ipc4_control_load_volume(sdev, scontrol); SND_SOC_TPLG_CTL_BYTES returns sof_ipc4_control_load_bytes(sdev, scontrol); SND_SOC_TPLG_CTL_ENUM and ENUM_VALUE return sof_ipc4_control_load_enum(sdev, scontrol); any other info_type returns 0 without touching scontrol. It returns the loader's value unchanged and does nothing else itself. For the bytes loader, its three argument checks at the start (max_size too small, priv_size above max_size, nonzero priv_size below the ABI header size) return -EINVAL before ipc_control_data is allocated, so on those paths nothing is freed or set to NULL; after the allocation, the ABI magic and size mismatch errors free the control data on the err path.
note: sof-ipc4-topology.c:2954-2971 (slice cut the head). Reviewer right: the early -EINVAL returns in sof_ipc4_control_load_bytes (ipc4-topology.c:2881-2900) occur before kzalloc (2909), so they neither free nor NULL ipc_control_data; only the later error paths use err. Loader internals beyond line 2939 not read.

name: sof_ipc4_check_reply_status
prose: Precondition: sdev is the SOF device, status is the reply status word. It masks status with SOF_IPC4_REPLY_STATUS and returns 0 if the result is 0. Otherwise it logs the status with its text from the ipc4_status table (or "Unknown" if not listed) and maps the masked status to an errno: 2 and 15 give -EOPNOTSUPP; 8, 11, 105 to 109, 114 to 115, 160 to 163 and 165 give -ENOENT; 4, 150 and 151 give -EBUSY; every other nonzero value gives -EINVAL. It returns that errno.
note: ipc4.c:85-130. Reviewer mechanical (contract omits the error codes): right; contract left empty because of the log call and table.

name: sof_pcm_trigger
prose: Precondition: component, substream and cmd for a SOF front-end PCM. Returns 0 immediately for a back-end (dai_link->no_pcm). Returns -EINVAL if snd_sof_find_spcm_dai finds no spcm. Otherwise it clears spcm->pending_stop for the stream before looking at cmd, so this happens even for an unhandled command. Then by cmd: PAUSE_PUSH sets ipc_first; PAUSE_RELEASE sets ipc_first if pcm_ops->ipc_first_on_start is set; START first checks suspend_ignored, which if set is cleared and the function returns 0, and otherwise sets ipc_first like PAUSE_RELEASE; SUSPEND returns 0 after setting suspend_ignored when pcm_ops->d0i3_supported_in_s0ix is set, system_suspend_target is SOF_SUSPEND_S0IX and the stream is d0i3_compatible (all three conditions are needed), else (in DSP-less mode it also sets reset_hw_params) it falls through to STOP, which sets ipc_first and sets reset_hw_params when pcm_ops->reset_hw_params_during_stop is set; any other cmd logs and returns -EINVAL. If ipc_first is not set it calls snd_sof_pcm_platform_trigger first; then, if pcm_ops->trigger exists, ret = pcm_ops->trigger. Afterwards, for PAUSE_RELEASE and START with ipc_first and ret 0 it calls the platform trigger; for SUSPEND, PAUSE_PUSH and STOP it calls the platform trigger (even if ret is an error) unless pcm_ops->platform_stop_during_hw_free is set, and for STOP with that flag it sets pending_stop for the stream. Finally, if ret is 0 and reset_hw_params is set it returns the result of sof_pcm_stream_free(..., false); otherwise it returns ret.
note: slice cut the head; real function pcm.c:326-436. Reviewer right on both points: pending_stop is cleared at 347 before the cmd switch, and the SUSPEND early return requires pcm_ops->d0i3_supported_in_s0ix (376-378).

name: sof_resume
prose: Precondition: dev is the SOF device; runtime_resume selects the runtime or system path. Returns 0 or a negative error. It returns 0 at once if the matching DSP callback (resume or runtime_resume) is not set, and returns 0 if sdev->first_boot is still set (the DSP was never started). Otherwise the DSP itself is resumed first with snd_sof_dsp_runtime_resume or snd_sof_dsp_resume; a negative result is logged and returned. In DSP-less mode it sets the firmware state to SOF_DSPLESS_MODE and returns 0. For a system resume on a platform with set_power_state, when the old power state was SOF_DSP_PM_D0, it resumes the trace (a failure is only a warning) and returns 0. Otherwise it sets SOF_FW_BOOT_PREPARE, loads the firmware (failure: state SOF_FW_BOOT_FAILED, error returned), sets SOF_FW_BOOT_IN_PROGRESS, runs the firmware (failure: SOF_FW_BOOT_FAILED, error returned), resumes the trace (non-fatal warning only), restores the pipelines through tplg_ops->set_up_all_pipelines if present (failure goes to setup_fail), resumes the clients, and calls the IPC pm op ctx_restore if present (a failure is only logged but ret keeps the negative value). At setup_fail it caches the debugfs contents when ret is negative (only with CONFIG_SND_SOC_SOF_DEBUG_ENABLE_DEBUGFS_CACHE) and returns ret, which is a negative error after a pipeline restore or ctx_restore failure and otherwise 0 or the last trace-resume result.
note: sof pm.c:73-194. Reviewer MIXED: right that the DSP resume callback is called before the DSP-less and D0 returns (96-109); wrong that a trace-resume error is returned: trace resume failures are non-fatal warnings (118-122, 154-160). The ret from the last trace resume can still be returned if later steps are skipped; read at 154-160 and 193: with no tplg_ops and no ctx_restore the function returns the trace-resume result (negative if that failed).

name: sof_suspend
prose: Precondition: dev is the SOF device; runtime_suspend selects the runtime or system suspend callback. Returns 0 or a negative error. It returns 0 immediately if the matching DSP suspend or runtime_suspend callback (sof_ops(sdev)->suspend or ->runtime_suspend) is not set. If the topology tear_down_all_pipelines op exists and the DSP power state is SOF_DSP_PM_D0 it tears down all pipelines (result ignored). If the firmware state is not SOF_FW_BOOT_COMPLETE it jumps to the suspend label. Otherwise: for system suspend it calls snd_sof_dsp_hw_params_upon_resume and returns its negative error; it then suspends the firmware trace (sof_fw_trace_suspend) and the clients (sof_suspend_clients) with the target state, and jumps to suspend if the target state is SOF_DSP_PM_D0 (so the trace and client suspend happen before that D0 check); otherwise it caches debugfs on runtime suspend when CONFIG_SND_SOC_SOF_DEBUG_ENABLE_DEBUGFS_CACHE is set, and if the IPC pm op ctx_save exists it calls it: -EBUSY and -EAGAIN are logged and returned, other negative results are only warned. At the suspend label it returns 0 if the firmware state is SOF_FW_BOOT_NOT_STARTED (no platform suspend then); else it calls snd_sof_dsp_runtime_suspend or snd_sof_dsp_suspend(target_state), logs a negative result, returns that result without resetting state if the target state is SOF_DSP_PM_D0, and otherwise resets the firmware state to SOF_FW_BOOT_NOT_STARTED, clears enabled_cores_mask and returns the result of the platform suspend call.
note: pm.c:196-294. Reviewer MIXED: right that trace and client suspend run before the D0 skip (238-245); the claim that nothing is suspended when firmware was not started holds only for fw_state SOF_FW_BOOT_NOT_STARTED (272-273); for other non-complete states the code jumps to suspend and does call the platform suspend.

name: sof_suspend
prose: Precondition: dev is the SOF device; runtime_suspend selects the runtime or system suspend callback. Returns 0 or a negative error. It returns 0 immediately if the matching DSP suspend or runtime_suspend callback (sof_ops(sdev)->suspend or ->runtime_suspend) is not set. If the topology tear_down_all_pipelines op exists and the DSP power state is SOF_DSP_PM_D0 it tears down all pipelines (result ignored). If the firmware state is not SOF_FW_BOOT_COMPLETE it jumps to the suspend label. Otherwise: for system suspend it calls snd_sof_dsp_hw_params_upon_resume and returns its negative error; it then suspends the firmware trace (sof_fw_trace_suspend) and the clients (sof_suspend_clients) with the target state, and jumps to suspend if the target state is SOF_DSP_PM_D0 (so the trace and client suspend happen before that D0 check); otherwise it caches debugfs on runtime suspend when CONFIG_SND_SOC_SOF_DEBUG_ENABLE_DEBUGFS_CACHE is set, and if the IPC pm op ctx_save exists it calls it: -EBUSY and -EAGAIN are logged and returned, other negative results are only warned. At the suspend label it returns 0 if the firmware state is SOF_FW_BOOT_NOT_STARTED (no platform suspend then); else it calls snd_sof_dsp_runtime_suspend or snd_sof_dsp_suspend(target_state), logs a negative result, returns that result without resetting state if the target state is SOF_DSP_PM_D0, and otherwise resets the firmware state to SOF_FW_BOOT_NOT_STARTED, clears enabled_cores_mask and returns the result of the platform suspend call.
note: pm.c:196-294; the packet slice (pm.c:269-389) starts at the suspend label, but the whole function was read. Reviewer WRONG for the function: the code does check the callbacks (207-211), call snd_sof_dsp_hw_params_upon_resume (226-232) and ctx_save (253-266); the reviewer's statement only matches the tail starting at the suspend label.

name: sun8i_codec_get_bclk_div
prose: Precondition: sysclk_rate, lrck_div_order and sample_rate are unsigned values; sample_rate must not be 0 (it is the divisor and is not checked). It computes div = (sysclk_rate / sample_rate) >> lrck_div_order, scans the constant table sun8i_codec_bclk_div in order and returns the val field of the first entry whose div equals the computed div, or -EINVAL if there is none. No side effects.
note: sun8i-codec.c:536-551. Reviewer mechanical (contract omits EINVAL): right; contract left empty because of the table lookup and the unchecked division.
